items: Senator Francis Pangilinan questioned the credibility of Davao City Assessor Jaime Adalin during the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, highlighting inconsistencies in his testimonies regarding property declarations.

Adalin initially confirmed that a property owned by Duterte's husband matched the residential lot declared in her SALN, but later expressed uncertainty when presented with photographs of the property.

MANILA, Philippines – Senator-judge Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan on Monday, November 9, questioned the credibility of a Davao City assessor over what he described as “inconsistent” testimonies during the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.

On Day 40 of the trial, Pangilinan questioned the shifting answers of Davao City Assessor Jaime Adalin, who initially said that a property bought by Duterte’s husband, lawyer Manases Carpio, in Davao matched the “residential lot” declared in the Vice President’s 2024 Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALN). The 379-square-meter property was acquired under a transfer certificate of title (TCT) ending in 0775.

“When you were testifying earlier, you said that the two properties in the SALN and the property description in the deed of sale were one and the same…but after the photos were shown, you were not sure,” Pangilinan said.
“How can you say you were sure the properties matched if you did not recognize the property in the photos?” he added.

Duterte is being tried for Article II, which involves allegations of unexplained wealth. Part of the accusations in the impeachment article are the undeclared properties in Duterte’s 2024 and 2025 SALNs.

The prosecution had previously alleged that Duterte failed to declare two properties in Davao: a lot in Matina, Davao City, which Carpio purchased for P6 million in July 2024, and a property in the Island Garden City of Samal, acquired for P3 million in 2018.

The defense, however, maintained that the properties were properly declared in Duterte’s SALN, while the prosecution questioned whether the land title cited by the defense corresponds to the property listed in the Vice President’s SALN.

During the trial, Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis “Chiz” Escudero asked Adalin whether the P10-million property listed in Duterte’s 2024 SALN was the same as Carpio’s property covered by the TCT ending in 0775. Adalin initially answered in the affirmative, citing similarities in the figures appearing in the tax declarations.
However, when the prosecution presented photographs of a commercial building in the said residential lot, the assessor expressed uncertainty about its identification.

Adalin later explained that the photograph without the business signage matched the image submitted to his office by its appraisers. But he could not confirm whether the restaurant named “Prime Bistro,” as shown in other photos, was the same property, as the photographs in their records did not bear any signage.

“So, in other words, when you said you are sure the properties were the same, you are actually not sure? Because when the photos were shown, you said you are unsure, and now, after discussing with your staff, you changed your answer. Why are your answers shifting?” Pangilinan said.
“Just an observation that, clearly, there are inconsistencies in your testimony. Forgive me, Engineer, but you say one thing, and then you say another thing,” he added.

During questioning by Senator-judge Bam Aquino, Adalin also acknowledged that he had not checked all of Duterte’s properties in Barangay 74-A despite his earlier confirmation that the properties in the SALN and transfer certificate matched.

“I was unable to check all of her properties because the subpoena only specified the title ending 0775,” Adalin said, adding that his office could submit an official document detailing the couple’s properties in the area if required by the impeachment court.
He was also asked if he had determined how many properties Duterte owned in the barangay.
“I’m not sure, although if we’re required to submit an official document, we will produce, as required,” he added. – Rappler.com
